summary: Octal formatting allocates floor(usize::BITS / 3) digit slots, causing an out-of-bounds panic when formatting a full usize-width element. The historical fix adds the remainder to provide sufficient capacity; it does not use the imported description's zip-based truncation implementation. The buffer-sizing reversal is exact and unique. Blocked: the fix adds no tests, and the existing slice::traits::format::octal test uses only u8 elements, requiring at most three digit slots and therefore missing the overflow. Searching Rust sources at the fixed commit found no detecting upstream test.

reversal.parent_text: const W: usize = <usize as BitMemory>::BITS as usize / $blksz;
